subject: gargoyle
pitch:
Category: Monster.
Subject: cathedral gargoyle crouched on a ledge.
Style: gothic stone carving.
reasoning:
I'm planning a moderately sized module for a crouched stone gargoyle on a small ledge, facing forward with haunches back, forelimbs planted, and wings positioned—aiming for solid quality within a manageable ~300 lines of code.

I'm sketching the skeleton hierarchy now: hips as the root joint, a spine chain curving from the hips up to the chest using catmull points, then a neck chain branching off the spine toward the head, carefully tracking parent-child joint relationships and coordinate placement for each segment.

I'm defining the head and jaw joints with aim targets for orientation, then sketching how the body geometry gets built -- sweeping the spine chain for the torso with varying radii, adding sphere parts for chest and haunches to give it a blocky stone look, and planning a mottled grey stone material with countershading.

For the legs, I'm placing hip joints for the haunches and using limb constructors with target feet positions and knee-bend hints to get a crouched stance, working out the foot and knee placement relative to the ledge height.

Now I'm adding sweep legs with foot boxes and claw-like toe spikes pointing forward from the ankle, then working out shoulder-to-hand arm chains with lengths and positions that keep the planted-hand distance close to straight, adjusting hand depth slightly for a better fit.

For the elbows, I'm bending them backward and outward using IK pole hints parented to the spine joint, with hand tips getting three claw spikes for fingers. Then I'm setting up the folded wing structure behind the shoulders as a shoulder-elbow-wrist chain with membrane fingers, defining the wing polyline points for the arm bones.

Still working out the membrane geometry...

Still defining wing points...

Now I'm working out the skull: a boxy head attached to the head bone, with a brow ridge above the eyes and frustum-shaped upper and lower jaws tapering out to the snout.

Still building head details... fangs spiking from both jaws, posing the jaw bone open by rotating it forward, then moving on to carving glowing amber eyes with slit pupils using an SVG decal texture.

I'm placing the eye spheres under the brow ridge, layering a dark socket sphere behind a smaller amber glowing one, with a box for the brow. Now I'm sketching curved bezier sweeps for the horns, defining base, control, and tip points that arc back and up from the skull.

Next I'm working out the ears as pointed spike shapes extruding outward from the head, then adding a row of spine ridge spikes along the body sweep, oriented along tangent frames for the dorsal ridges.

Now I'm defining the neck and chest sweeps, belly sweep radii tapering along the spine curve, haunch and shoulder spheres positioned at the hips and shoulders, and starting a curling tail chain that sweeps down and back along the ledge.

Still mapping tail bones...

Adding a quatrefoil decal plane on the ledge front as a carved stroke texture, skipping the waterspout idea but maybe darkening the mouth hollow, then placing toe claws and ankle foot boxes at the chain tip joint.

Still writing stone paint logic...

Checking total height with horns and wings against the ledge scale — comes to about 1.45m, which works fine for a 1.15m gargoyle body. Now working out the wing pose, with the left wing angled outward on the positive x side.

Setting up the skeleton joints — head, jaw, spine chain, and neck. Working through the neck joint positions, parenting them to the spine's last joint, and placing the head joint and its bounding box so the eyes sit correctly on the front face.

Now I'm positioning the jaw and snout: calculating the head box front face at z=.61, placing the brow and amber eyes just inside that, and defining the snout and jaw frustum boxes with fangs positioned near the front of the mouth.

Next I'm placing the nostril spheres at the snout tip, adding a small chin spike for a beard, and defining horn bases with curved control points sweeping up from the skull, plus ear spikes angled outward from the sides of the head.

Now I'm defining the color palette (stone, dark, horn, claw, amber tones) and a darker membrane shade, then setting up flat box-geometry shading, an eye glow effect, and a quatrefoil SVG motif made of overlapping circles.

Working out the ledge and plane dimensions, placing side planes at offset positions, and calculating exact y-coordinates for foot and hand targets so limbs rest naturally on the stand surface.

Checking that the hip height sits correctly above the ledge lip, and sinking the tail slightly into the surface for a more grounded look using sphere-based haunch parts with flat shading. Time to write the final version.
